title: v00 · Baseline (first A+ mix)
banner_span: First lab × commercial mix — historical baseline
h1:
An applied AI lab
building the company
that runs itself.
lead: Autonomica is a living experiment: one founder, systems that act, and the tools required to make autonomous business real — proven on our own operations and on client volume.
sub: The lab ships work, not whitepapers. Today that means distributed batch AI for industrial workloads and white-glove embeds that install force multipliers inside real companies.
lab_p: Most companies use AI as a helper inside human workflows. We’re testing what happens when systems own the loop — decide, act, course-correct — and when volume work is engineered for unit economics instead of demos.
Client work is not a side shop. It’s how the lab stays honest: real data shapes, real cost pressure, real failure modes.
pillars: AI owns execution loops. Humans set direction and handle true edge cases — not every approval.
For batch work, $/item is a design input: model ladders, distribution, retries, QC sampling.
White-glove embeds find where human time is the bottleneck and install systems that multiply capacity.
Findings and patterns leave the lab as blueprints over time — the experiment is meant to transfer.
applied_h2:
What the lab ships
into the world.
applied_p: Two engagement surfaces — framed as applied research tracks, not SKUs. Same standards: production systems, measured outcomes, no pilot theater.
applied_mono: // applied tracks · funded by real workloads · feed the autonomy thesis

tracks.title: Distributed workload automation
tracks.desc: Custom AI systems for large-volume batch processing. We design cost-efficient, distributed pipelines for work that can be sharded, queued, and completed at scale — transcription, OCR, image generation and manipulation, or any distributable AI job where unit economics decide whether the system is real.
tracks.side: Industrialize a known high-volume workload with architecture built around cost and throughput.

tracks.title: White-glove AI-fication
tracks.desc: We embed into a company, learn how work actually moves, and install force-multiplier systems — not a transformation deck. Discovery with operators, highest-leverage interventions first, production handoff so outcomes stick without us forever.
tracks.side: Join the org long enough to find leverage and leave working systems behind.

classes: Multi-hour media, model ladders, multilingual routing, cost under load.
Archives and forms at volume — layout-aware pipelines, sampling QC.
Bulk generation, transforms, automated QC; humans only on edges.
If it shards and has a quality bar, the lab can industrialize it.
exp_p: Autonomica itself is the long experiment — a company evolving as we learn what autonomous business looks like. Applied client work funds the path and stress-tests every claim.
phases: Build the AI stack and ship applied systems — batch workloads and embeds — that pay for what comes next.
Functions transfer from human to AI, starting with the highest-volume, most repetitive loops.
The AI runs the company. The founder steps back to strategy and edge cases.
Publish blueprints so others can run the same playbook without starting from zero.
collab_h2:
Bring a workload.
Or bring the company.
collab_p: Short notes are enough: volume and formats, cost pressure, quality bar — or “we need a force multiplier in X” and where humans are still the bottleneck.
You’re not buying a catalog item. You’re funding applied work inside a lab that measures success in production systems.
collab_note: Prefer a call? Book 30 minutes — same topics: batch systems or white-glove embed.
form_engage: Not sure — help the lab choose

title: v01 · Thesis-first
banner_span: Autonomy manifesto leads · applied tracks as evidence
lead: An applied AI lab running a single experiment at company scale: can one founder and a stack of acting systems outrun the old model of hire-to-grow?
sub: We don’t sell a catalog. We run the experiment in public — and take on hard batch workloads and deep company embeds because that’s where the thesis either holds or breaks.
lab_h2:
AI shouldn’t wait
for a human to click approve.
lab_p: At most companies, AI drafts and suggests. A person still owns every decision that matters. That’s autocomplete with a budget line.
Autonomica tests the opposite: systems that execute inside clear boundaries, founders who set direction, and volume pipelines engineered so cost doesn’t kill the idea at scale.
pillars: Receive, decide, act, review — without a human in the middle of every step.
If it only works on a demo file, it isn’t a system. Batch work exposes reality.
Embeds aim at force multipliers: more output without proportional hiring.
The endgame isn’t a black-box service. It’s replication — blueprints others can run.
applied_num: 02 · Where the thesis meets the world
applied_p: Two ways outsiders plug into the lab. Both produce production systems. Both feed what we learn about autonomous business.
applied_mono: // evidence tracks · the lab stays honest by shipping

tracks.title: Distributed workload automation
tracks.desc: When the problem is volume — millions of minutes, pages, or images — we design distributed AI systems around unit cost. Transcription, OCR, image generation and manipulation, or any job that can be sharded. The thesis dies if the economics don’t work; so we start there.
tracks.side: Stress-test AI systems under load and cost — not slideware.

tracks.title: White-glove AI-fication
tracks.desc: When the problem is the company itself, we embed. Sit with operators, find where human time is pure friction, install systems that multiply capacity, and leave ownership behind. Force multipliers — not a tool dump.
tracks.side: Prove leverage inside a living organization.

classes: Fleets, ladders, languages — cost that survives the second million minutes.
OCR and extraction that complete, with QC that doesn’t re-humanize everything.
Generate, transform, score — humans on the exceptions only.
If it distributes and has a quality bar, it’s in scope.
exp_p: Autonomica is the lab notebook. Applied work pays for the next page and forbids comfortable theory.
phases: Stack + applied systems that fund the experiment and prove basic loops.
Hand functions to AI, highest-volume first.
Company runs; founder on strategy and edges.
Publish the playbook. Others shouldn’t rebuild from myth.
collab_p: Send a workload with volume and cost pressure — or invite an embed where leverage is stuck behind humans.
You’ll get production systems. We’ll get evidence. That’s the deal.
collab_note: Calendar works too. Thirty minutes is enough to see if the fit is real.

title: v02 · Operator-direct
banner_span: Plain speech · agents + research first · batch as equal evidence
h1:
An applied AI lab
building companies
that run themselves.
lead: One founder, production systems, and a public experiment: can autonomous operations outrun hire-to-grow? We don’t sell a catalog — we ship agents and systems that execute, then publish what we learn.
sub: Today that means custom agent creation and deployment — landscape research, competition monitoring, content, website ops — and distributed batch AI when volume and unit cost are the constraint. Same bar: production only, no pilots.
lab_h2:
AI shouldn’t wait
for a human to click approve.
lab_p: Most “AI” still drafts and waits. Autonomica tests the opposite: agents and systems that execute inside clear boundaries, while we run our own company as the long experiment in autonomous operations.

Client work is research under pressure — real functions, real volume, real failure modes. We won’t run a six-week demo that dies in a shared drive. If it ships, it has owners, metrics, and a cost model. Patterns that hold get published.
pillars: Receive, decide, act, review — without a human in the middle of every step.
Research, competition, content, site ops — company functions as deployed agents, not chat windows.
When the job is bulk AI, unit cost is architecture. Batch work exposes what demos hide.
The endgame isn’t a black box. It’s replication — blueprints and findings others can run.

h1:
An applied lab
with two engines
and one thesis.
lead: Thesis: autonomous business is buildable. Engine one: industrialize batch AI until unit cost is honest. Engine two: embed until companies feel a real force multiplier.
sub: Autonomica runs both engines on purpose — client volume and deep embeds keep the autonomy experiment from becoming a blog.
lab_h2:
One experiment.
Two ways it pays rent.
lab_p: The long project is Autonomica itself: a company increasingly run by systems that act. That only stays real if we keep touching volume and organizations outside our own walls.
So the lab has two engines — not a product menu. Each engine produces production systems and returns evidence to the thesis.
pillars: Systems own loops; founders own direction.
Distributed AI for shardable volume, designed on $/item.
What we learn in either engine changes how we run Autonomica.
applied_p: Pick an engine. You’re not buying a SKU — you’re attaching real constraints to the experiment.

tracks.title: Distributed workload automation

title: v05 · Lab notebook
banner_span: First-person lab voice · intimate · still commercial-clear
h1:
We’re building
a company that
doesn’t need us
in every loop.
lead: This is the lab notebook for that attempt. Autonomica is the experiment: applied AI, production systems, and a bias toward work that either scales or teaches us why it won’t.
sub: Right now the notebook has two recurring chapters: batch systems for brutal volume, and white-glove embeds where we move in long enough to install a force multiplier.
lab_p: We got tired of AI stories that never meet a queue depth or a finance team. So we run systems on our own work and on other people’s volume until the story has numbers.
If you work with us, you’re not a “customer logo.” You’re a chapter — with constraints that keep us honest.
pillars: We care about systems that executed, not decks that performed.
Every batch note includes how unit cost was designed — or where it broke.
Embeds start with operators, not org charts.
When a pattern repeats, it leaves the notebook as a blueprint.
applied_p: Two ongoing lines of applied work. Same lab. Different contact surfaces.

tracks.title: Distributed workload automation
tracks.desc: We design and ship custom AI pipelines for large-volume batch work — transcription, OCR, image generation and manipulation, and other distributable jobs. The plot is always the same: can this stay correct when the queue is deep and the budget is real?
tracks.side: Bring the volume. We’ll write the system.

tracks.title: White-glove AI-fication
tracks.desc: We embed. We watch how work moves. We install force multipliers and stay until the handoff is real. These chapters are messier — organizations are — and they’re where we learn what autonomy looks like around humans, not instead of pretending they vanish.
tracks.side: Bring the bottleneck. We’ll move in.

classes: If it shards, we can open a chapter.
exp_p: Short chapters fund the long book: a company that largely runs without a human in every loop — and notes clear enough for someone else to follow.
phases: Tools, batch muscle, embed craft — enough to fund the next year.
Our own functions move onto systems, one loop at a time.
We’re mostly out of the operational path.
collab_p: A pile of media. A document mountain. An image factory. A team that can’t hire its way out.
Write a short note. If there’s a chapter here, we’ll say how we’d run it.
collab_note: Happy to talk live — 30 minutes, no pitch theater.
